overview: This single-page Department of State list-of-papers sheet records an April 4, 1941 telegram concerning the status of the Kwantung Leased Territory. Citing information from the consul at Dairen, the entry clarifies that Japan’s lease permitted it to exercise jurisdictional and administrative authority in the territory, but that the United States did not regard the area as an integral part of the Japanese Empire; it also directs readers to file 894C.5151/8.

subfiles.title: List of Papers entry on the status of the Kwantung Leased Territory
subfiles.about: An archival listing summarizes an April 4, 1941 telegram clarifying the United States position on Japanese authority and sovereignty in the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: The sheet records a telegram dated April 4, 1941, numbered 015, concerning the Kwantung Leased Territory. Information attributed to the consul at Dairen distinguishes Japan’s jurisdictional and administrative powers under the lease from territorial incorporation into the Japanese Empire. The entry states that the United States did not consider the territory an integral part of Japan and provides a cross-reference to 894C.5151/8.

interest: The entry succinctly documents the important diplomatic distinction between Japan’s de facto administrative authority in the Kwantung Leased Territory and internationally recognized sovereignty over it. It is useful for tracing the State Department’s legal understanding of Japan’s position in Manchuria and for locating the related substantive telegram through the cross-reference to 894C.5151/8. The consul’s intervention “in the interest of accuracy” also shows how consular reporting could correct or refine the Department’s territorial terminology.
